icd10_codes.description: Displaced fracture of shaft of right clavicle, initial encounter for closed fracture
Other motorcycle driver injured in noncollision transport accident in traffic accident, initial encounter
State road as the place of occurrence of the external cause

dialogue:
[doctor] hey , {PATIENT_FIRST} , nice to meet you . i'm doctor {DOCTOR_LAST} .
[patient] hey , nice to meet you .
[doctor] hey , dragon , i'm seeing {PATIENT_FIRST} {PATIENT_LAST} , he's a {AGE}-year-old male here for a right shoulder injury . so what happened ?
[patient] so i wrecked my motorcycle on saturday . me and my buddy {OTHER_FIRST} were riding up to {PLACE} , just a weekend ride , and we were on the state route that goes up through the hills . it's a two-lane road with a lot of curves .
[doctor] okay .
[patient] and i came around a curve and there was a bunch of gravel spread across my lane . i hit it , and the back tire just slid out from under me . i laid the bike down and slid , and i landed right on my right shoulder .
[doctor] okay . so no other vehicles were involved ? you did n't hit a car or anything ?
[patient] no , nobody else . it was just me and the gravel .
[doctor] were you wearing a helmet ?
[patient] yeah , full face helmet , and my jacket .
[doctor] good . did you hit your head ?
[patient] the helmet hit the road a little , but i did n't black out or anything . i remember the whole thing .
[doctor] any headache , nausea , blurry vision since then ?
[patient] no .
[doctor] okay . and where is the pain exactly ?
[patient] it's like right here , on the collarbone . there's a big bump there now .
[doctor] okay . and how bad is the pain ?
[patient] like a seven . it's really bad when i try to lift my arm .
[doctor] any numbness or tingling in your arm or your fingers ?
[patient] no , my hand feels fine .
[doctor] okay . any other injuries ? any pain in your chest , your ribs , your hips ?
[patient] just some road rash on my right forearm , like scrapes , but the jacket took most of it . my buddy cleaned it up .
[doctor] okay . did you go to the emergency room ?
[patient] no , i probably should have . i just put my arm in a sling i had at home and took some advil .
[doctor] okay . do you have any medical problems ?
[patient] no , not really .
[doctor] do you smoke ?
[patient] yeah , about a pack a day .
[doctor] how long have you been smoking ?
[patient] since i was like 16 .
[doctor] okay . so i do wanna talk to you about that , because smoking actually slows down bone healing quite a bit .
[patient] really ? i did n't know that .
[doctor] yeah . have you ever tried to quit ?
[patient] i tried once with the gum . i made it about a month . i get cravings first thing in the morning , i usually light one up within like 10 minutes of waking up .
[doctor] okay . would you be interested in trying again ?
[patient] yeah , i mean , if it's gonna help this heal , i'll try .
[doctor] okay . let's take a look at you . so , on exam , there's an obvious deformity over the middle of the right clavicle , with swelling and bruising . the skin is intact , it's not tented . i'm gonna press here gently .
[patient] ow , yeah .
[doctor] okay . tender over the midshaft clavicle . can you wiggle your fingers ? squeeze my hand . good . you have good pulses at the wrist , and sensation is normal in the hand . there are some healing abrasions on the right forearm , they look clean , no signs of infection .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] hey , dragon , show me the right clavicle x-ray . so here's your x-ray . you can see the collarbone is broken right in the middle , and the two ends are shifted , so it's a displaced midshaft fracture of the right clavicle . there's about one centimeter of shortening , and it's not in a lot of pieces .
[patient] do i need surgery ?
[doctor] so for most of these , we treat them without surgery . since yours is displaced but not too shortened , i think we can try a sling first . we'd consider surgery if it's shortened more than about two centimeters , if the skin was at risk , or if it does n't heal .
[patient] okay . how long am i gonna be out of work ? i'm an electrician , so i kinda need both arms .
[doctor] probably light duty only for at least six weeks , no climbing ladders or overhead work .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] so i want you in the sling for comfort for the next two to three weeks . you can take it off to do gentle elbow , wrist and hand movement . no lifting anything heavier than a coffee cup with that arm , and absolutely no riding the motorcycle until it's healed .
[patient] yeah , the bike's pretty beat up anyway .
[doctor] for pain , you can take ibuprofen 600 milligrams every six hours with food , and tylenol in between . for the smoking , i'm gonna start you on nicotine patches , 21 milligrams a day , and you can use the nicotine gum for cravings . and i'll give you the number for the quit line .
[patient] okay , sounds good .
[doctor] we'll get another x-ray in two weeks to make sure it has n't shifted .
[patient] all right . thanks , doc .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Right shoulder pain after motorcycle accident.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

{PATIENT_FIRST} {PATIENT_LAST} is a {AGE}-year-old male who presents with right clavicle pain after a motorcycle accident on Saturday.

The patient was the driver of a motorcycle on a two-lane state road during a weekend ride when he lost control on gravel in a curve. The rear tire slid out and he laid the bike down, landing on his right shoulder. No other vehicles were involved. He was wearing a full-face helmet and riding jacket. His helmet struck the road, but he denies loss of consciousness, headache, nausea, or blurry vision. He reports pain over the right collarbone with a visible bump, rated 7/10, worse with arm elevation. He denies numbness or tingling. He also sustained abrasions to the right forearm. He did not seek emergency care. He has been using a sling and Advil.

SOCIAL HISTORY

Smokes 1 pack per day since age 16. Smokes within 10 minutes of waking. Previously tried nicotine gum with 1 month of abstinence. He is interested in quitting. He works as an electrician.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Right shoulder: Obvious deformity over the midshaft of the right clavicle with swelling and ecchymosis. Skin intact, not tented. Tender to palpation over the midshaft clavicle.
Neurovascular: Radial pulse intact. Sensation intact in the hand. Full finger motion and grip.
Skin: Healing abrasions on the right forearm, clean, without signs of infection.

RESULTS

X-ray of the right clavicle: Displaced midshaft clavicle fracture with approximately 1 cm of shortening. No comminution.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Displaced fracture of the shaft of the right clavicle, closed.
- Nonoperative management with sling for comfort for 2 to 3 weeks.
- Gentle elbow, wrist, and hand range of motion.
- Light duty at work for at least 6 weeks.
- No lifting with the right arm. No motorcycle riding until healed.
- Ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours with food, alternating with Tylenol.
- Repeat x-ray in 2 weeks. Surgical fixation would be considered for shortening greater than 2 cm, skin compromise, or nonunion.

2. Nicotine dependence, cigarettes.
- Counseled that smoking delays fracture healing.
- Start nicotine patch 21 mg daily with nicotine gum as needed for cravings.
- Quit line information provided.
